**DNA damage** (stated probability 0.62); key evidence e2, e4, e13, e10, e9.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is favoured, not tied. Single-well atlas (e5) was 4/10 vs 4/10, but the pooled four-well atlas (e13) is 7/10 DNA damage vs 3/10 DNA replication with higher mean similarity (0.792 vs 0.737), supported by dose-dependent nuclear enlargement (e10, rho=+1.00), raised integrated DNA, reduced counts and intact cytoskeleton on phenotype review (e4). This excludes microtubule, actin and mitotic classes better than it separates the two DNA classes, so DNA replication remains a credible runner-up. Probability 0.62 is therefore calibrated rather than overconfident. Each dose is single-replicate, but the graded response across four doses corroborates the high-dose well; one further well or free re-analysis is unlikely to materially separate DNA damage from replication arrest, which would require a molecular assay outside this imaging panel.

## Unblinding

Compound: **chlorambucil** (PubChem CID [2708](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/2708))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The high-dose acquisition drove the correct call: massive hypertrophy with cell_area z=+12.0 and nuc_area z=+9.9, plus raised integrated DNA and lower density with intact cytoskeleton on phenotype review, fit DNA accumulation rather than mitotic or cytoskeletal disruption. The pooled four-well atlas shifting to 7/10 DNA damage vs 3/10 DNA replication and the monotonic nuclear enlargement with rho=+1.00 corroborated that pattern across doses.

What misled was how close DNA replication remained: the first single-well atlas was tied 4/10 vs 4/10, and even at the end DNA replication held 0.28 probability. With single replicates per dose, trends like DNA content rho=+0.80 p=0.2 and cell-count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 were directionally right but underpowered, so imaging alone could not fully separate G2 DNA-damage arrest from S-phase block.

The choice to sample 10, 0.3, 3 and 1 uM to map gradient was useful for excluding microtubule, actin and kinase classes, but it left the DNA damage vs replication tie to be broken only by the median atlas comparison. Probability 0.62 was appropriately calibrated for that residual ambiguity, and unblinding as chlorambucil, a DNA inhibitor, confirmed the ranking.

What was right:
- High-dose hypertrophy (cell_area z=+12.0, nuc_area z=+9.9, nuc_solidity z=+6.5 in e2) with raised nuc_dna_integrated z=+4.1 in e8 pointed to DNA accumulation, not mitotic arrest
- Dose-dependent nuclear enlargement (e10 rho=+1.00) with falling cell counts (e12 rho=-0.80) and lower density plus intact cytoskeleton on phenotype review (e4) favored a DNA-acting class
- Pooled four-well atlas in e13 at 7/10 DNA damage vs 3/10 DNA replication correctly broke the early e5 tie of 4/10 vs 4/10 toward DNA damage

What was wrong or missed:
- Early single-well atlas (e5) and hypothesis update left DNA damage and DNA replication tied at 0.42, failing to separate G2 arrest from replication block
- Relied on single replicates per dose with non-significant dose trends (e9, e11, e12 p=0.2), leaving DNA replication at 0.28 as a credible runner-up
- No molecular readout was acquired in-run to distinguish break-induced arrest from S-phase inhibition, so the 0.62 confidence appropriately reflected residual DNA-vs-DNA ambiguity

Proposed next experiment: Stain for gamma-H2AX foci plus EdU pulse-chase and phospho-H3 flow cytometry to test DNA-break G2 arrest versus S-phase replication block.
